startup.name: Orthogonal
startup.description: Orthogonal is a marketplace and payment layer where AI agents discover, access and pay for APIs on a pay per use basis, with no subscriptions or sales calls. API providers list once and get paid each time an agent calls them. Two person team in San Francisco. Revenue would come from a take rate on API calls. Protocol work such as Coinbase x402 and Stripe machine payments is emerging as of the start date.

yc_acceptance.basis: The company was accepted to YC, which is the premise of the test, so acceptance is near certainty. For reference the random applicant prior is about 1 percent, and agent infrastructure with a technical two person team is squarely in a hot YC theme, but the pitch has no stated traction or distribution.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly say no because a two sided marketplace for API calls needs providers and agent developers at the same time, and protocol builders like Coinbase and Stripe were releasing agent payment standards that could make a neutral aggregator unnecessary. No traction or take rate evidence is stated in the input. The acceptance step is set from the premise that the company was admitted.

ladder.why_it_fails: The most likely failure is that nobody can see real call volume. Agents mostly call a handful of big APIs with keys the developer already holds, so a marketplace of long tail APIs has little demand, and investors wait for proof. Stripe and Coinbase can offer the same pay per call primitives directly. Analogs: magic-2 raised a seed and then shut down, and plasticity, an API startup, was acquired after a small seed.

ladder.why_it_fails: At B investors want real transaction volume and defensible network effects. The most likely miss is that standards commoditize the payment layer, so the take rate collapses toward zero, and the large payment companies bundle agent payments into existing accounts that developers already use, which leaves no room for a separate vendor at Series B scale.

ladder.why_it_fails: Late rounds need a business that large payment networks cannot absorb. The likely failure is that Stripe, Coinbase, Cloudflare or a model lab owns agent payments and API discovery, leaving little standalone value. A small take rate on a still small market may never justify a late stage valuation.

outcomes.why_it_fails: The most likely end is a stall or a small acquihire by a payments, API gateway or agent infrastructure company. A large outcome needs agent API spend to grow enormously and this layer to stay independent of Stripe, Coinbase and the model vendors that set the protocols.

killers.risk: Stripe, Coinbase or Cloudflare own agent payments
killers.evidence: Coinbase created x402 and Stripe added an x402 preview and its own machine payments work, which cover pay per call directly.
killers.mitigation: Build on top of the standards and own API discovery and billing aggregation.

killers.risk: Two sided cold start between API providers and agent developers
killers.evidence: The marketplace needs listings and agents at the same time and no volume is stated.
killers.mitigation: Seed supply with popular APIs and give agents free credits.

killers.risk: Agent API spend stays small and concentrated
killers.evidence: One analysis notes that agent payments have almost no real volume yet and developers already hold keys for major APIs.
killers.mitigation: Focus on one agent framework with real usage.

killers.evidence: Open protocols make the payment layer a commodity and compress what a middle layer can charge.
killers.mitigation: Sell discovery, monitoring and budgets rather than just payment.

competition_now.what: Preview letting developers charge agents for API and HTTP requests in USDC.
competition_now.traction: Preview launched with open source tooling.

competition_now.name: Status quo: API keys and monthly subscriptions
competition_now.what: Developers sign up and manage keys per vendor.

technical_complexity.rationale: A proxy, metering and billing layer plus a catalog is buildable by two strong engineers in a quarter. Harder parts are trust, fraud, refunds and compliance in payments, and integrating many APIs with different authentication schemes.

takeover_risk.rationale: Large payment and infrastructure players already ship pay per call primitives and have distribution to every developer. A rival can add API discovery within months, so independence depends on moving faster in discovery and supply.

evidence.claim: Coinbase and Stripe are both backing HTTP 402 based protocols for agents paying for APIs.
Agent payments are described as early with little volume so far.

narrative.headline: A hot idea that big payment players are building directly, so seed is likely and later rounds depend on real volume.
narrative.general_summary: Orthogonal lets agents discover and pay for APIs per call. The theme is hot and Coinbase and Stripe both launched agent payment protocols, which validates the need but also shows who the competition is. A seed above the YC check is slightly more likely than the B2B anchor because of the theme. Later rounds need real transaction volume, a defensible take rate and a neutral position against giants that can add the same features. The ladder follows the anchors with small adjustments, and most paths end in a stall or a small acquihire.
